record.context_brief: TV convergence in stationary ergodic G/G/m FCFS
record.original_question: Consider the multi-server first-come-first-served queue G/G/m with interarrival times {(t_n)} and service times {(sigma_n)} such that the two-dimensional sequence {(sigma_n, t_n)} is stationary ergodic, the stability condition E sigma_1 < m E t_1 holds, and the Kiefer-Wolfowitz workload vector starts from the zero initial value. Is it true that, under these assumptions alone and without any further mixing or regenerative condition, the distribution of the workload vector converges in total variation to a stationary distribution as n tends to infinity?

evidence.quote: The conjecture is: assuming only that the sequence {(sigma_n, t_n)} is stationary ergodic, that the stability condition holds, and that the initial value is 0, then there is no need for any further restriction to establish the convergence in the total variation.
sup_A |P(W_n in A) - pi(A)| -> 0, n -> infinity.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a first-come-first-served queue with $m\ge 1$ identical parallel servers. Customers are indexed by $n\in\mathbb{Z}$; customer $n$ arrives at time $T_n=\sum_{k<n} t_k$, where $t_n>0$ is the interarrival time between customers $n$ and $n+1$, and requires service time $\sigma_n>0$. Assume the bivariate sequence $\{(\sigma_n,t_n)\}_{n\in\mathbb{Z}}$ is stationary and ergodic on some probability space, with $\mathbb{E}\sigma_1<\infty$, $\mathbb{E}t_1<\infty$, and the stability condition
$$\mathbb{E}\sigma_1 < m\,\mathbb{E}t_1.$$
Let $W_n=(W_n^{(1)},\dots,W_n^{(m)})\in\mathbb{R}_+^m$ denote the Kiefer–Wolfowitz workload vector at the arrival epoch of customer $n$, with components arranged in non-decreasing order. It satisfies the recursion
$$W_{n+1}=R\bigl((W_n+\sigma_n e_1 - t_n \mathbf{1})^+\bigr),$$
where $e_1=(1,0,\dots,0)$, $\mathbf{1}=(1,1,\dots,1)$, $(\cdot)^+$ is componentwise positive part, and $R$ reorders coordinates in non-decreasing order. Assume the initial condition $W_0=0$.

Under the stability condition there exists a stationary distribution $\pi$ on $\mathbb{R}_+^m$ to which the workload vector converges weakly along the Loynes construction. Question: is it always true, under only the assumptions above (stationarity and ergodicity of $\{(\sigma_n,t_n)\}$, the stability condition, and $W_0=0$), and without imposing any additional mixing, regenerative, or independence assumption, that
$$\sup_{A\subset \mathbb{R}_+^m}\bigl|\mathbb{P}(W_n\in A)-\pi(A)\bigr|\;\longrightarrow\;0\qquad\text{as }n\to\infty,$$
that is, the law of $W_n$ converges to $\pi$ in total variation?
artifact.status_search_result: Searches for follow-up work resolving this conjecture (TV-convergence of the Kiefer–Wolfowitz workload vector in stationary ergodic G/G/m FCFS queues without further mixing assumptions) did not surface a definitive resolution. Related results address convergence under additional mixing or regenerative structure, but a confirmation or refutation of the conjecture in full generality could not be verified from the available sources.

status_evidence.title: Some Open Problems Related to Stability (arXiv:0909.0462)
status_evidence.snippet: Paper discussing open problems in queueing theory relating to stability.
status_evidence.claim: The question is posed as an open problem in a list of open problems on stability.

status_evidence.title: The existence of fixed points for the .GI/1 queue (Annals of Probability)
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses ergodic fixed points and stationary regimes for queues with stationary input.
status_evidence.claim: Related literature treats stationary regimes and convergence under further assumptions, but does not establish TV-convergence in the fully general stationary ergodic G/G/m setting.
